# `stackspirit` CLI reference

Status: current

<!-- generated by docs/reference/generate.py; do not edit -->

> **VOWP compatibility.** `vowp` is the compatibility alias of `stackspirit`: it has the same
> command tree and the same flags, and every command below also works as `vowp <command>`. The
> command help text still prints the original `vowp` program name in places.

This page is the complete `--help` tree of the `stackspirit` binary, committed as text. The command
surface is `V0_1_COMMANDS` plus `V0_2_COMMANDS` in
[`crates/vowp-cli/src/cli.rs`](../../crates/vowp-cli/src/cli.rs); the behaviour of each command is
specified in [`docs/design/cli.md`](../design/cli.md). Hidden commands are included because they
are part of the binary even when `stackspirit --help` does not advertise them.

Regenerate after a CLI change:

```sh
cargo build -p vowp-cli --bin stackspirit
python3 docs/reference/generate.py
python3 docs/reference/check-reference.py
```

## `stackspirit`

```text
StackSpirit (formerly VOWP): local-first supervisor for AI coding agents

Usage: stackspirit [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  init          Initialise this git repository as a VOWP project
  doctor        Check the node, database, harnesses and providers
  up            Create the tmux layout and start the supervisor
  down          Stop the supervisor
  status        Show the supervisor, jobs, slots, limits, cost and inbox
  board         Print or refresh the board
  plan          Start a planner turn for a goal
  job           Add, inspect or change jobs
  graph         Print, export or import the job graph
  attach        Attach to a job's tmux window
  session       List and operate universal sessions
  chat          Alias of `session chat`
  inbox         List and answer inbox items
  cost          Show cost totals
  node          Add, list or remove nodes
  offload       Show the effective offload policy or the offload read model
  loops         List or pause supervisor loops
  schedule      Manage scheduled actions
  promote       Promote a change to an environment
  rollback      Roll a release back
  releases      List releases
  reindex       Rebuild the session index from JSONL logs
  backup        Back up the node database
  schema        Print one exported JSON Schema
  project       Register, list, pause or archive projects
  fleet         Read the node snapshot, queue and inbox
  capacity      Show, change or reload measured capacity
  secret        Set, list, remove or request secrets
  gc            List lifecycle classes and collect garbage
  tunnel        Open, list or close control-machine SSH tunnels
  setup         Plan or apply the AI-first setup
  control       Configure this machine as the control machine
  orchestrator  Create and manage orchestrator sessions
  migrate       Migrate a v0.1 home to the v0.2 layout
  home          Link or move the home between the StackSpirit and legacy directory names
  mcp           Run the stdio MCP server or the Mac-side proxy
  agent         Enroll, run or inspect the Mac-side agent
  surface       Create, list or revoke a paired local surface; `--node` names the surface's node
  version       Print the binary version

Options:
      --json                 Print one machine-readable JSON document on stdout
      --node <NAME>          Run the command on that node over ssh
      --project <NAME|PATH>  Project name or path; defaults to the nearest ancestor with `stackspirit.toml` or `vowp.toml`
      --home <DIR>           Node home (default `$STACKSPIRIT_HOME`, then `$VOWP_HOME`, else `~/.stackspirit` or `~/.vowp`)
      --no-color             Disable colour even when stdout is a terminal
  -q, --quiet                Suppress non-essential human output
  -v, --verbose...           Increase log verbosity (`-v`, `-vv`)
  -h, --help                 Print help
  -V, --version              Print version
```

### `stackspirit init`

```text
Initialise this git repository as a VOWP project

Usage: stackspirit init [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --json                 Print one machine-readable JSON document on stdout
      --name <NAME>          Project name slug; defaults to the repository directory name
      --force                Overwrite an existing project and existing framework files
      --node <NAME>          Run the command on that node over ssh
      --no-framework         Do not install the embedded framework files
      --project <NAME|PATH>  Project name or path; defaults to the nearest ancestor with `stackspirit.toml` or `vowp.toml`
      --home <DIR>           Node home (default `$STACKSPIRIT_HOME`, then `$VOWP_HOME`, else `~/.stackspirit` or `~/.vowp`)
      --no-color             Disable colour even when stdout is a terminal
  -q, --quiet                Suppress non-essential human output
  -v, --verbose...           Increase log verbosity (`-v`, `-vv`)
  -h, --help                 Print help
```

### `stackspirit up`

```text
Create the tmux layout and start the supervisor

Usage: stackspirit up [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --foreground           Run the supervisor loop in this process
      --json                 Print one machine-readable JSON document on stdout
      --detach               Explicitly detach (the default)
      --node <NAME>          Run the command on that node over ssh
      --no-tmux              Do not create the tmux windows
      --project <NAME|PATH>  Project name or path; defaults to the nearest ancestor with `stackspirit.toml` or `vowp.toml`
      --home <DIR>           Node home (default `$STACKSPIRIT_HOME`, then `$VOWP_HOME`, else `~/.stackspirit` or `~/.vowp`)
      --no-migrate           Do not migrate the home before starting the supervisor
      --no-color             Disable colour even when stdout is a terminal
      --once                 Run exactly one supervisor tick and exit
  -q, --quiet                Suppress non-essential human output
      --replace              Drain a running supervisor, apply pending migrations and start this binary
  -v, --verbose...           Increase log verbosity (`-v`, `-vv`)
  -h, --help                 Print help
```

### `stackspirit down`

```text
Stop the supervisor

Usage: stackspirit down [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --drain                Let active runs and gate tasks finish; admit no new work
      --json                 Print one machine-readable JSON document on stdout
      --force                Send SIGTERM if the supervisor does not stop by itself
      --node <NAME>          Run the command on that node over ssh
      --kill-windows         Kill the tmux windows too
      --project <NAME|PATH>  Project name or path; defaults to the nearest ancestor with `stackspirit.toml` or `vowp.toml`
      --home <DIR>           Node home (default `$STACKSPIRIT_HOME`, then `$VOWP_HOME`, else `~/.stackspirit` or `~/.vowp`)
      --no-color             Disable colour even when stdout is a terminal
  -q, --quiet                Suppress non-essential human output
  -v, --verbose...           Increase log verbosity (`-v`, `-vv`)
  -h, --help                 Print help
```

#### `stackspirit job add`

```text
Add one job and its brief

Usage: stackspirit job add [OPTIONS] --id <SLUG> --title <TEXT> --kind <KIND>

Options:
      --id <SLUG>              Job id slug
      --json                   Print one machine-readable JSON document on stdout
      --node <NAME>            Run the command on that node over ssh
      --title <TEXT>           Human-readable title
      --kind <KIND>            Job kind (`build`, `verify`, `plan`, ...)
      --project <NAME|PATH>    Project name or path; defaults to the nearest ancestor with `stackspirit.toml` or `vowp.toml`
      --home <DIR>             Node home (default `$STACKSPIRIT_HOME`, then `$VOWP_HOME`, else `~/.stackspirit` or `~/.vowp`)
      --role <ROLE>            Role; defaults from the kind
      --no-color               Disable colour even when stdout is a terminal
      --profile <NAME>         Profile; defaults to the role name
      --needs <A,B>            Jobs that must finish first
  -q, --quiet                  Suppress non-essential human output
      --owns <GLOB,...>        Ownership globs
  -v, --verbose...             Increase log verbosity (`-v`, `-vv`)
      --reads <GLOB,...>       Read globs
      --gates <SET|SHORT,...>  Gate set names or short gate forms
      --priority <N>           Dispatch priority (higher first)
      --max-attempts <N>       Maximum fix rounds
      --brief-file <PATH>      Read the brief body from this file
      --brief <PATH|->         Read the brief body from stdin (`-`)
      --placement <PLACEMENT>  Offload placement: `home`, `any`, `node:<name>` or `node:<name>+home`
  -h, --help                   Print help
```

#### `stackspirit job update`

```text
Change a job's editable fields

Usage: stackspirit job update [OPTIONS] <ID>

Arguments:
  <ID>  Job id

Options:
      --json                   Print one machine-readable JSON document on stdout
      --title <TEXT>           New title
      --node <NAME>            Run the command on that node over ssh
      --priority <N>           New priority
      --profile <NAME>         New profile
      --project <NAME|PATH>    Project name or path; defaults to the nearest ancestor with `stackspirit.toml` or `vowp.toml`
      --home <DIR>             Node home (default `$STACKSPIRIT_HOME`, then `$VOWP_HOME`, else `~/.stackspirit` or `~/.vowp`)
      --owns <GLOB,...>        Replacement ownership globs
      --no-color               Disable colour even when stdout is a terminal
      --reads <GLOB,...>       Replacement read globs
      --gates <SET|SHORT,...>  Replacement gates
  -q, --quiet                  Suppress non-essential human output
      --add-needs <A,B>        Needs to add
  -v, --verbose...             Increase log verbosity (`-v`, `-vv`)
      --remove-needs <A>       Needs to remove
      --note <TEXT>            Free-form note
  -h, --help                   Print help
```

#### `stackspirit session export`

```text
Export a session bundle or ASIF package

Usage: stackspirit session export [OPTIONS] <ID>

Arguments:
  <ID>
          Session id or unique prefix

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>
          Interchange format

          Possible values:
          - bundle: Native `vowp-bundle-v1` JSON. The default for both commands
          - asif:   ASIF 0.4 (review draft) package. Semantic interchange with declared losses
          
          [default: bundle]

      --json
          Print one machine-readable JSON document on stdout

      --node <NAME>
          Run the command on that node over ssh

  -o, --out <FILE|->
          Output file (default `./<id>.vowp-bundle.json`, or `./<id>.asif.zip` for ASIF); `-` writes to stdout

      --project <NAME|PATH>
          Project name or path; defaults to the nearest ancestor with `stackspirit.toml` or `vowp.toml`

      --tail <N>
          Number of tail events to include (bundle only)

      --home <DIR>
          Node home (default `$STACKSPIRIT_HOME`, then `$VOWP_HOME`, else `~/.stackspirit` or `~/.vowp`)

      --redact <LITERAL>
          Replace this exact literal with `<redacted>` (ASIF only, repeatable)

      --no-color
          Disable colour even when stdout is a terminal

      --redact-file <FILE>
          Read exact redaction literals from a local file, one per line (ASIF only)

      --keep-host-paths
          Keep host-path-looking strings in a trusted local export (ASIF only)

  -q, --quiet
          Suppress non-essential human output

      --report <FILE>
          Keep the full `vowp-asif-report-v1` document at this file (ASIF only)

  -v, --verbose...
          Increase log verbosity (`-v`, `-vv`)

      --strict
          Refuse `Blocking` and `Integrity` ASIF losses (ASIF only)

      --allow-loss
          Let recoverable ASIF integrity/ambiguity problems become declared losses (ASIF only)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

#### `stackspirit session import`

```text
Import a session bundle or ASIF package

  <FILE>
          Bundle/package file, document, directory, or `-` for stdin

          Interchange format

          Possible values:
          - bundle: Native `vowp-bundle-v1` JSON. The default for both commands
          - asif:   ASIF 0.4 (review draft) package. Semantic interchange with declared losses

      --json

      --node <NAME>
          Node to import on

      --executor <EXECUTOR>
          Executor for the child session (bundle only)

          Project name or path; defaults to the nearest ancestor with `stackspirit.toml` or `vowp.toml`

      --cwd <DIR>
          Working directory

      --home <DIR>
          Node home (default `$STACKSPIRIT_HOME`, then `$VOWP_HOME`, else `~/.stackspirit` or `~/.vowp`)

      --no-color
          Disable colour even when stdout is a terminal

      --same-id
          Keep the bundle's session id; refuse when it already exists locally (bundle only)

      --branch <ID>
          Select one ASIF branch when the document has more than one (ASIF only)

  -q, --quiet
          Suppress non-essential human output

      --report <FILE>
          Keep the full `vowp-asif-report-v1` document at this file (ASIF only)

  -v, --verbose...
          Increase log verbosity (`-v`, `-vv`)

      --strict
          Refuse `Blocking` and `Integrity` ASIF losses (ASIF only)

          Let recoverable ASIF integrity/ambiguity problems become declared losses (ASIF only)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

### `stackspirit gc`

```text
List lifecycle classes and collect garbage

Usage: stackspirit gc [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --apply
          Delete eligible files instead of only reporting

      --json
          Print one machine-readable JSON document on stdout

      --class <CLASS>
          Restrict to one lifecycle class

      --node <NAME>
          Run the command on that node over ssh

      --older-than <DURATION>
          Collect closed sessions and run output older than this window (for example 7d, 36h, 2w).

      --project <NAME|PATH>
          Project name or path; defaults to the nearest ancestor with `stackspirit.toml` or `vowp.toml`

      --home <DIR>

          Clock override for tests (RFC 3339)

          Disable colour even when stdout is a terminal

  -q, --quiet
          Suppress non-essential human output

          Increase log verbosity (`-v`, `-vv`)

          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

#### `stackspirit orchestrator attach`

```text
Attach a desktop UI as the session owner, then hold the lease until stdin closes

Usage: stackspirit orchestrator attach [OPTIONS] --holder <NAME> <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>  Orchestrator name

Options:
      --holder <NAME>        Holder name shown to other surfaces, for example `opencode-desktop`
      --json                 Print one machine-readable JSON document on stdout
      --label <LABEL>        Friendly surface label, for example `StackSpirit · macbook`
      --node <NAME>          Run the command on that node over ssh
      --project <NAME|PATH>  Project name or path; defaults to the nearest ancestor with `stackspirit.toml` or `vowp.toml`
      --takeover             Take the session over from a live owner
      --home <DIR>           Node home (default `$STACKSPIRIT_HOME`, then `$VOWP_HOME`, else `~/.stackspirit` or `~/.vowp`)
      --no-color             Disable colour even when stdout is a terminal
  -q, --quiet                Suppress non-essential human output
  -v, --verbose...           Increase log verbosity (`-v`, `-vv`)
  -h, --help                 Print help

Prints the one-time grant, then heartbeats the lease until stdin reaches end-of-file and releases it. Keep this process (as a child of the UI) alive while the UI writes. Recorded ownership is cooperative: it does not stop a UI that calls the app's HTTP API directly. --node is not an SSH redirect; attach works only on a home-hosted orchestrator.
```

```text
      --kind <KIND>          Which state directory `--move` moves: `home` (default), `agent` or `control` [default: home]
      --dry-run              Print the plan and write nothing
      --no-color             Disable colour even when stdout is a terminal
  -q, --quiet                Suppress non-essential human output
      --yes                  Confirm the changes
      --no-link              With `--move`: do not leave a symlink at the old path
  -v, --verbose...           Increase log verbosity (`-v`, `-vv`)
  -h, --help                 Print help
```

```text
      --env <NAME>           Name of the one variable to inject
      --json                 Print one machine-readable JSON document on stdout
      --node <NAME>          Run the command on that node over ssh
      --project <NAME|PATH>  Project name or path; defaults to the nearest ancestor with `stackspirit.toml` or `vowp.toml`
      --home <DIR>           Node home (default `$STACKSPIRIT_HOME`, then `$VOWP_HOME`, else `~/.stackspirit` or `~/.vowp`)
      --no-color             Disable colour even when stdout is a terminal
  -q, --quiet                Suppress non-essential human output
  -v, --verbose...           Increase log verbosity (`-v`, `-vv`)
  -h, --help                 Print help
```
